Altamont.lead: Altamont is a small town in Duchesne County. It sits along State Route 87 and serves as the hub of the Upper Country. It was established as a central location for a new high school, and its name combines those of nearby Altonah and Mount Emmons.
sources: Establishment year: Harvest of Memories: 1905 to 1988
Name origin: Utah Place Names, by John W. Van Cott

sections.title: Town Government and Services
sections.html: The Town of Altamont has a mayor and town council. It's served by the Upper Community Recreation District and the Upper Country Water Improvement District.

sections.title: Public Safety
sections.html: Law enforcement is provided by the Duchesne County Sheriff's Office. Altamont also has a fire department, which it shares with the other Upper Country communities.

sections.title: Community Events
sections.html: Longhorn Days, held around Pioneer Day in mid-to-late July, is Altamont's biggest yearly celebration, with a rodeo, parade, pageant, fireworks show and week of activities.

sections.title: Parks and Recreation
sections.html:
Altamont's park features a playground, ball diamonds, outdoor basketball courts, a pavilion and restrooms. Altamont also has a rodeo arena off State Route 87 just west of town.

The Altamont War Veterans Memorial honors those from the area who've served their country. The memorial is located in front of Altamont High.

sections.title: Cemetery
sections.html: The Altamont-Mount Emmons Cemetery is located off State Route 87 just west of town.

sections.title: Schools
sections.html: Altamont Elementary School serves kindergarten–6th grade. A new elementary school is being built to replace the current one. Altamont High School serves 7th–12th grade. It was rebuilt in 2012. The schools belong to the Duchesne County School District.

sections.title: Library
sections.html: The Duchesne County Library hosts library nights in Altamont for returns, pickups, checkouts and opening new accounts. There's also a library drop box at the Upper Country Market.

sections.title: Church
sections.html: Altamont is home to the Altamont Stake Center, which serves the members of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints in Altamont and surrounding communities. The stake center also hosts a family history center. A seminary building serves the high school's Latter-day Saint students.

sections.title: Healthcare
sections.html: Altamont is home to a small medical clinic, with limited hours, operated by Uintah Basin Healthcare. Hospital, emergency and other medical services are available in Roosevelt, 18 miles away.

sections.title: Businesses and Services
sections.html:
Altamont is the commercial, religious and educational center of the Upper Country communities of Altonah, Boneta, Bluebell, Mount Emmons, Mountain Home, Talmage and Upalco, along with Arcadia.

Upper Country Market is a grocery store with hardware and sporting goods sections. The store features a hot and cold case deli for grab-and-go meals. It also hosts a branch of Mountain America Credit Union, open three days a week. The only gas station in town is Swasey's Other Place, a Sinclair station.

Trent's Grill serves burgers, fries, drinks, ice cream and more. The Bluebell Store & Grille, another nearby dining option, serves breakfast, lunch and dinner.

Altamont Motel is a small hotel with rooms containing kitchenettes. The Mountain Home Lodge and Falcon's Ledge offer additional lodging options close to Altamont.

Altamont Theatre is a recently renovated movie theater showing classic movies and holding plays, classes and other events. Country Flair is a western-themed clothing boutique focused on women's clothing. Altamont is also home to Branded Boutique and Salon, a hair salon that carries women's clothing.

Altonah.lead: Altonah, a scattered community located in Duchesne County's Upper Country, was first surveyed in 1906. Originally called Alexander, it received its current name, for its high elevation, in 1912.
sources: Name origin, founding and survey dates: Utah Place Names, by John W. Van Cott

sections.title: Government and Services
sections.html: Altonah is served by the Upper Country Water Improvement District and the Upper Community Recreation District. Altonah is also the location of a U.S. Forest Service guard station, used as employee housing and as a work site.

sections.title: Public Safety
sections.html: Altonah is served by the Altamont Fire Department and the Duchesne County Sheriff's Office. The Ute Tribal Police Department has jurisdiction over tribal land within the Uintah and Ouray Reservation.

sections.title: Parks and Recreation
sections.html: Nearby Altamont has a park and rodeo arena.

sections.title: Cemetery
sections.html: Altonah has its own cemetery.

sections.title: Schools
sections.html: Kindergarten–12th grade students from Altonah attend elementary and high school in Altamont. The schools are part of the Duchesne County School District.

sections.title: Churches
sections.html: Altonah Latter-day Saints are split between attending the Lake Fork Ward, with its chapel in Boneta, and the Altamont First Ward, with its chapel in the stake center. Both wards are located within the Altamont Stake.

sections.title: Businesses and Services
sections.html: Hidden Springs Ranch is a lodge in Altonah available for large reunions and retreats. The lodge features a cabin, pond, pool and other recreation facilities.

Arcadia.lead: Arcadia is a scattered community in Duchesne County. It was first settled in 1906 and previously called Red Cap, after a Ute leader. Its current name comes from the Arcadian region of Greece.
sources: Name origin, founding and survey dates: Utah Place Names, by John W. Van Cott

sections.title: Government and Services
sections.html: Arcadia is part of the Upper Community Recreation District and within the boundaries of the East Duchesne Culinary Water Improvement District.

sections.title: Public Safety
sections.html: Law enforcement is provided by the Duchesne County Sheriff's Office. Fire service is provided by the Myton Fire Department. The Ute Tribal Police Department has jurisdiction over tribal land within the Uintah and Ouray Reservation.

sections.title: Cemetery
sections.html: The old Red Cap Cemetery is located in Arcadia.

sections.title: Businesses and Services
sections.html: Chuck's Meats maintains a processing plant in Arcadia. Its retail store is located in Duchesne.

Bluebell.lead: Bluebell is a small community in Duchesne County, located near Altamont. The Gales were the first family to settle the town in 1907. Others joined in 1908. School began in a granary in 1909, and a church house opened in 1910. The town was named for the wildflowers growing in the area.
sources: Settlement dates: Early history of Duchesne County, compiled by Mildred Miles Dillman
Name origin: Utah Place Names, by John W. Van Cott
Cemetery dates: UGRC (CC-BY-4.0)

sections.title: Government and Services
sections.html: Bluebell is served by the Upper Country Water Improvement District and the Upper Community Recreation District.

sections.title: Public Safety
sections.html: Bluebell is served by the Duchesne County Sheriff's Office and the Altamont Fire Department. The Ute Tribal Police Department has jurisdiction over tribal land within the Uintah and Ouray Reservation.

sections.title: Community Events
sections.html: Bluebell's Independence Day celebration includes a breakfast and flag ceremony at the park. The Bluebell Corn Maze also draws visitors to the town each fall.

sections.title: Parks and Recreation
sections.html: The Bluebell Community Park has a pavilion, playground, sports field, volleyball pit, basketball court and walking track.

sections.title: Cemetery
sections.html: The Bluebell Cemetery, which dates to 1913, lies just west of town.

sections.title: Schools
sections.html: Bluebell's young people attend elementary and high school in Altamont, as part of the Duchesne County School District.

sections.title: Church
sections.html: The Bluebell Ward of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints holds meetings at the stake center in Altamont.

sections.title: Businesses and Services
sections.html: The Bluebell Store & Grille was established as a general store in 1915. Today, it hosts a convenience store, post office and grill that serves breakfast, lunch and dinner.

Boneta.lead: Boneta is located west of Altamont along Utah State Route 87 in Duchesne County. To the north lies Mountain Home, and further west is Talmage. Boneta was settled in 1907 and named for the Spanish word “bonita,” meaning beautiful.
sources: Name origin, founding and survey dates: Utah Place Names, by John W. Van Cott

sections.title: Government and Services
sections.html: Boneta is served by the Upper Country Water Improvement District and the Upper Community Recreation District.

sections.title: Public Safety
sections.html: Boneta is served by the Duchesne County Sheriff's Office and the Altamont Fire Department. The Ute Tribal Police Department has jurisdiction over tribal land within the Uintah and Ouray Reservation.

sections.title: Parks and Recreation
sections.html: Altamont, nearby, has a park and rodeo arena.

sections.title: Cemetery
sections.html: Boneta shares a cemetery with Mountain Home.

sections.title: Schools
sections.html: Boneta's students attend school at Altamont elementary and high school as part of the Duchesne County School District.

sections.title: Church
sections.html: Boneta is home to the Latter-day Saint meetinghouse for Boneta, Talmage, Mountain Home and parts of Altonah. It's part of the Altamont Utah Stake.

sections.title: Businesses and Services
sections.html:
The Kinder Morgan Altamont natural gas liquids plant, in Boneta, processes 80 million cubic feet per day of natural gas, condensing out 4,000 barrels per day of liquid byproducts (from the methane natural gas) and separating them into propane, butane and C5+.

Quilts N Fabrics, on 18750 W. (head south from the natural gas plant), sells fabric in-shop and online. It also offers in-person quilting classes and open sewing.

Bridgeland.lead: Bridgeland, in Duchesne County, is located along the Duchesne River, 10 miles east of the town of Duchesne. Bridgeland is a scattered community along River Road, which branches from Highway 40 west of Myton and reconnects in Duchesne. To the north of Bridgeland is Arcadia. Settled in 1908, Bridgeland was named for the metal truss bridge that spanned the river there.
sources: Name origin: Utah Place Names, by John W. Van Cott
Cemetery dates: UGRC (CC-BY-4.0)

sections.title: Government and Services
sections.html: Bridgeland is part of the East Duchesne Culinary Water Improvement District.

sections.title: Public Safety
sections.html: Bridgeland is served by the Duchesne County Sheriff's Office and the Duchesne Fire Department. The Ute Tribal Police Department has jurisdiction over tribal land within the Uintah and Ouray Reservation.

sections.title: Cemetery
sections.html: Bridgeland has its own cemetery, located along the road to Arcadia. It dates to 1922.

sections.title: Schools
sections.html: Bridgeland students attend elementary and high school in Duchesne. The schools are part of the Duchesne County School District.

sections.title: Church
sections.html: Bridgeland has a Latter-day Saint meetinghouse where the Bridgeland Ward meets. It's part of the Duchesne Stake.

Cedarview.lead: Cedarview is a small community, located in Duchesne County, along the Neola Highway, halfway between Roosevelt and Neola. Cedarview shares connections with Crescent, Montwell and Monarch. Cedarview was once a fledgling town with stores, blacksmith shops, two schools, a post office, a creamery and a ward house. It's named for the juniper-covered hills it overlooks.
sources: Community history: Early history of Duchesne County, compiled by Mildred Miles Dillman
Name origin: Utah Place Names, by John W. Van Cott
Cemetery dates: UGRC (CC-BY-4.0)

sections.title: Government and Services
sections.html: The Cedarview-Montwell Special Service District provides culinary water service to the area.

sections.title: Public Safety
sections.html: The community is served by the Duchesne County Sheriff's Office and the Roosevelt Fire Department. The Ute Tribal Police Department has jurisdiction over tribal land within the Uintah and Ouray Reservation.

sections.title: Cemetery
sections.html: The Cedarview Cemetery, which dates to 1912, is located off the Neola Highway, north of the Cedarview turnoff.

sections.title: Schools
sections.html: Cedarview students attend elementary school in Neola and junior high and high school in Roosevelt as part of the Duchesne County School District.

sections.title: Church
sections.html: Cedarview Latter-day Saints attend the Roosevelt 7th Ward, with its chapel in Neola. The ward is part of the Roosevelt West Stake.

Ioka.lead: Ioka is a scattered community, located between Highway 40 and Upalco along Utah State Route 87 (the stretch there is called Ioka Lane). Ioka was settled in 1907 and named after a Ute leader.
sources: Name origin, founding and survey dates: Utah Place Names, by John W. Van Cott
Cemetery dates: UGRC (CC-BY-4.0)

sections.title: Public Safety
sections.html: Most of Ioka is served by the Roosevelt Fire Department. The Ute Tribal Police Department has jurisdiction over tribal land within the Uintah and Ouray Reservation.

sections.title: Cemeteries
sections.html: Ioka has two cemeteries, both located on the bench south of the community: the Ioka Memorial Park (1926) and the Old Ioka Cemetery (1906).

sections.title: Schools
sections.html: Ioka students attend Centennial School, junior high and high school in Roosevelt. Ioka is located in the Duchesne County School District.

sections.title: Church
sections.html: The Ioka Ward of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints meets in Myton. It's part of the Roosevelt Stake.

Monarch.lead: Monarch is a small community north of Montwell and west of Neola in Duchesne County. It was named by Lee Brown, a local woman, who said the town would be the “monarch of all it surveyed.”
sources: Name origin: Utah Place Names, by John W. Van Cott

sections.title: Government and Services
sections.html: Monarch is part of the Cedarview-Montwell Special Service District and Neola Community Park District.

sections.title: Public Safety
sections.html: The Duchesne County Sheriff's Office covers law enforcement in the area. Fire service is provided by the Neola Fire Department. The Ute Tribal Police Department has jurisdiction over tribal land within the Uintah and Ouray Reservation.

sections.title: Parks and Recreation
sections.html: The Neola Community Park is located a few miles away.

sections.title: Cemetery
sections.html: Monarch has a small cemetery.

sections.title: Schools
sections.html: Monarch's school kids attend elementary in Neola and junior high and high school in Roosevelt. The community is located in the Duchesne County School District.

sections.title: Church
sections.html: Monarch is part of the Neola First Ward in the Roosevelt West Stake of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints.

Neola.lead: Neola is a town in Duchesne County, 10 miles north of Roosevelt. Founded in 1912, Neola's name is said to mean “last move” or “move no more” in a Native American language. Its location was chosen in place of another planned townsite called Packer, located two miles to the east. That plan was scrapped, and Packer's log schoolhouse was moved to Neola.
sources: Name origin: Utah Place Names, by John W. Van Cott
Townsite history: Early history of Duchesne County, compiled by Mildred Miles Dillman

sections.title: Government and Services
sections.html: The Neola Community Park District is a special service district managing the community's park and cemeteries. The Neola Water & Sewer District provides drinking water and sewer services in town.

sections.title: Public Safety
sections.html: The Neola Fire Department covers the Neola and Monarch areas. The Duchesne County Sheriff's Office provides law enforcement for the town. The Ute Tribal Police Department has jurisdiction over tribal land within the Uintah and Ouray Reservation.

sections.title: Community Events
sections.html: The Neola 4th of July Rodeo has been a town tradition since 1932. Besides the rodeo, the Neola 4th of July Celebration includes a parade, patriotic program and other activities.

sections.title: Parks and Recreation
sections.html: The Neola Community Park features a rodeo arena, pavilions, playgrounds, sand volleyball pits, a combination basketball-pickleball court, a ball diamond, a disc golf course and RV hookups.

sections.title: Cemeteries
sections.html: Neola has two cemeteries. To get to the Neola Cemetery, go one mile north of town, then turn and go one mile west. The older Greenhalgh Cemetery lies three miles north of town.

sections.title: Schools
sections.html: Neola Elementary School serves students in kindergarten–5th grade from Neola and the surrounding area. After fifth grade, students attend school at Roosevelt Jr. High and Union High in Roosevelt. The schools are located in the Duchesne County School District.

sections.title: Church
sections.html: The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints meetinghouse in Neola hosts three wards, covering Neola and surrounding communities. The congregations are part of the Roosevelt Utah West Stake.

sections.title: Businesses and Services
sections.html: Kett's Neola Store is a convenience store and gas station. It features grab-and-go breakfast and lunch, some fishing supplies, basic groceries and gift items.

Duchesne.lead: The town's first resident and merchant was A. M. Murdock. He had earlier come to the Basin to trade with the Indians in Whiterocks. He originally named the town Dora after his daughter. It was later renamed Theodore after President Roosevelt and finally Duchesne in 1911.
sources: Community history: Utah History Encyclopedia, by John D. Barton; A History of Duchesne County, by John D. Barton; Early History of Duchesne County, compiled by Mildred Miles Dillman

Fruitland.lead: Originally known as Rabbit Gulch, the town's name was changed to Fruitland to entice more settlers to the area.
sources: Name origin: Utah Place Names, by John W. Van Cott

add_sections.title: Businesses and Services
add_sections.html: Big G on 40 is a Sinclair gas station with convenience groceries and a cafe.

Hanna.lead: The area was briefly home to the Indian agency in the 1860s. Stockmore, in the Hanna area, was first settled in 1905. The town of Hanna is named for its first postmaster, William P. Hanna.
sources: Community history: A History of Duchesne County, by John D. Barton; Early History of Duchesne County, compiled by Mildred Miles Dillman
Name origin: Utah Place Names, by John W. Van Cott

add_sections.title: Businesses and Services
add_sections.html: Hanna Country Store stocks fuel, groceries, hardware items and fishing gear.

Myton.lead: Named in 1905 for Major H. P. Myton, former Indian agent at Fort Duchesne.
sources: Community history: A History of Duchesne County, by John D. Barton
Name origin: Utah Place Names, by John W. Van Cott
Myton.schools_html: Myton Elementary (kindergarten–5th) and Con Amore School (special education, prekindergarten–12th) are part of the Duchesne County School District. After elementary school, students attend junior high and high school in Roosevelt.

add_sections.title: Community Events
add_sections.html: Myton Daze is held at the end of June and includes a fair, parade, rodeo and fireworks.

section_html.trails: The Myton Ball Park Path is a paved walking path at the ballpark. It is about 0.2 miles long.

Roosevelt.lead: The town was named after Theodore Roosevelt. The area was previously known as Dry Gulch.
sources: Community history: Utah History Encyclopedia, by John D. Barton; A History of Duchesne County, by John D. Barton; Early History of Duchesne County, compiled by Mildred Miles Dillman

add_sections.title: Community Events
add_sections.html: Uintah Basin in Celebration (UBIC) is held each year the week before the first Saturday in August. The weeklong celebration includes entertainment, vendors, a parade, a pageant and other events.

Roosevelt.schools_html: East School (prekindergarten–5th), Centennial School (kindergarten–5th), Kings Peak School (kindergarten–5th), Roosevelt Jr High (6th–8th) and Union High (9th–12th) are part of the Duchesne County School District.

section_html.churches:
• Faith Baptist Church
  • Iglesia de Dios E.C. Casa del Alfarero (Spanish-language Pentecostal)
  • Roosevelt Baptist Church (Southern Baptist)
  • Roosevelt Christian Assembly (Assemblies of God)
  • Roosevelt Kingdom Hall (Jehovah’s Witnesses)
  • St. Helen Catholic Church
  • The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints (5 meetinghouses)
section_html.hospitals: Uintah Basin Healthcare operates the hospital and clinic in Roosevelt.
section_html.colleges: Uintah Basin Technical College and the Utah State University Uintah Basin campus are located in the city.

Tabiona.lead: Fort Tabby was built in 1860. Later, a town was founded in the area, first called Tabbyville or Tabby, and formally named Tabiona in 1915. Tabby was a Ute leader who was among the first to move with his people to the Uintah Reservation.
sources: Community history: Town of Tabiona; A History of Duchesne County, by John D. Barton; Early History of Duchesne County, compiled by Mildred Miles Dillman

add_sections.title: Community Events
add_sections.html: Tabiona's Fourth of July celebration includes a parade and rodeo.

add_sections.title: Businesses and Services
add_sections.html: Sagebrush Inn & Cafe is located in Tabiona.

add_sections.title: Businesses and Services
add_sections.html: Mountain Home Lodge has six rooms and a shared kitchen. It also has a small store with ice cream, and gas.
